# CLAUDE.md 31000 -> 32000, 2026-08-25, with owner sign-off and the reason on the record.
#
# What crossed it: `929fc42` added two lines to the Commands block -- a widened `ruff` scope
# that finally covers `.claude/operations/scripts/` and the new Codex-mirror gate. That is
# ~110 raw chars, which the x4 delivery weighting turns into ~440, and the file landed at
# 31272 against 31000. **The overrun was 68 RAW CHARACTERS.**
#
# Why raised rather than trimmed. The available trims are instruction text: the alternative
# was cutting ~70 chars of guidance an agent actually reads, to fit a round number, in the
# file most likely to be re-grown next week. The two new lines close a real CI scope gap --
# `fleet-sync.py` shipped with three type errors because the engine was outside every
# declared lint scope -- so they earn their weight.
#
# What this does NOT do: relax the ratchet. A raise is a decision on the record, exactly
# like a DISCLOSED_WIDENINGS entry, and the point of the gate is that it forces one. If the
# next 1000 chars arrive without a comparable justification, trim instead -- and the honest
# trim is to move content OUT of CLAUDE.md into the agent that consumes it, which the
# delivery weighting is designed to reward.
